items.title: Builder execution boundary
rules: Read and edit only the admitted isolated checkout and task-owned context.
On Windows PowerShell 5.1, every textual `Get-Content` read must use `-Encoding UTF8`; never rewrite source from mojibake console text.
Do not publish, install, activate, or mutate canonical workspace source; the trusted worker owns validation and Trial delivery.

items.title: Skill public SDK boundary and feedback
rules: Skill source may use public `adaos.sdk` contracts only; never import `adaos.services`, edit core, imitate a missing core contract locally, or depend on worker internals.

If the admitted SDK/API cannot express the requested behavior, stop that branch and return typed development feedback with the missing or unclear contract, impact, evidence, and the smallest useful capability request.

After an actual public method or resource application fails, include one bounded application trace with the exact contract and operation refs, redacted input summary, expected and observed behavior, validation result, and trace/test refs; never infer an execution trace from documentation review alone.
A model-proposed capability, path, permission, or owner is evidence for orchestration, not execution authority; the trusted worker resolves and admits it.

items.title: Skill WebUI and public tool contract
rules: For every added or changed same-skill WebUI `callSkill`, skill `dataSource`, or handler callable, reconcile the exact name across `webui.json`, `skill.yaml` `tools`, `exports.tools`, the entry/`@tool` handler, and complete input/output schemas in the same patch.

Do not conclude while a callable exists in code or UI but is absent from the public manifest graph. If a required counterpart is outside the authorized paths, stop and report that scope blocker instead of leaving a partial contract.
Browser-read tools require a bounded declared `data_route`; action acknowledgements stay compact and do not duplicate projected data. Keep duplicated skill/scenario UI contracts in parity.

items.title: Declarative UI state and identity
rules: Use stable unique IDs and canonical language-neutral refs for areas, widgets, actions, and domain targets; localized labels are presentation, never routing or storage identity.
Represent materially different page modes with `layout.variants`, and update the view mode plus selected identity atomically; do not stack competing main areas behind incidental visibility checks.
Preserve established interaction state and unrelated behavior. Dynamic IDs, renderer-private assumptions, and hidden client-only state are contract defects.

items.title: UI interaction and delivery states
rules: Declare initial focus, default action, stable action feedback, loading, empty, stale, permission-denied, unavailable, and retry behavior where the surface can encounter them.
Use stable typed resources and core delivery mechanisms for icons and media; do not embed machine-local paths or make decorative state carry domain meaning.
Preserve keyboard, focus, readable labels, and bounded responsive layout across modal and page surfaces.

items.title: Scenario composition boundary
rules: A scenario orchestrates skills, surfaces, NLU affordances, and bindings; do not hide reusable capability, external IO, long-running work, heavy state, or new permissions inside scenario data.

Declare required and optional skill dependencies and bind actions to real exported tools. Missing required capability blocks apply; missing optional capability needs an explicit degraded or guided-install state.
Keep scenario-owned state separate from skill-owned domain state, and do not let Prototype or Preview install, activate, or mutate live runtime.

items.title: Declarative workflow authority
rules: When a manifest references `workflow.json`, treat that admitted file as the workflow-definition authority; do not recreate transitions as independent Python or UI tables.
Preserve the complete TransitionDescriptor contract and validate the definition structurally through the public workflow boundary.
Keep runtime state, transition effects, and presentation projections separate from the immutable workflow definition.

items.title: Data route and receiver ownership
rules: Declare receiver ownership, route budget, causal read policy, and projection target explicitly.
Do not use Yjs as an unconstrained database or publish duplicate state through action responses and projections.
A route or projection mismatch is a validation failure, not a reason to add an undeclared fallback.

items.title: Receiver snapshot and stream pressure
rules: Declare one receiver owner, initial snapshot behavior, replay and reconnect semantics; subscription alone must not leave the first browser state unknowable.
Bound payload size, fanout, update rate, queue depth, and retained state, and coalesce high-frequency updates before projection.
Keep receiver callbacks idempotent and side-effect bounded; observable pressure may create non-blocking debt but must not silently corrupt state.

items.title: Causal tool-backed reads
rules: A tool-backed browser surface names the exact tool and a finite causal `read_policy`: semantic read key, allowed triggers, invalidation tags, rate budget, and last-value behavior.
Do not turn rerenders, unrelated actions, focus, generic state updates, or timers into reads. Explicit Retry reloads only the selected semantic read identity.
Keep the last valid value only when declared, and distinguish loading, stale, unavailable, permission-denied, and domain-empty states.

items.title: Typed resource and storage boundary
rules: Use typed AdaOS resource/provider contracts and owner-scoped SDK storage roots; declare typed query filters, sort/page limits, views, and allowed operations.
Do not let callers choose arbitrary filesystem roots or persist synthetic provider data as authoritative state. Unsupported filters and unavailable providers must be explicit, not silently ignored.
Create/update/delete and reload behavior must preserve optimistic revision, idempotency, authorization, event emission, and deterministic empty/unavailable/validation states.

items.title: Runtime lifecycle and failure evidence
rules: Keep activation, rehydrate, drain, and failure paths bounded, idempotent, and observable.
Validation and runtime failures must produce stable error codes, trace/retryability metadata, and bounded evidence; do not hide them behind synthetic success defaults or domain-empty UI.
A command acknowledgement is not proof that browser-visible state was delivered or that the selected runtime slot loaded the new handler.

items.title: Python import, dependency, and resource lifecycle
rules: Keep imports passive: no threads, model loads, sockets, subscriptions, external callbacks, publishes, or persistent writes at module import time.
Bound every cache and worker by items/bytes/time, give every thread, task, executor, subprocess, model, and callback one lifecycle owner plus drain/dispose cleanup, and keep reload idempotent.
Declare every imported dependency and its supported isolation boundary in `skill.yaml`; validate against the authoritative manifest schema instead of relying on Builder's environment.

items.title: Event loop and blocking isolation
rules: `async` does not make blocking SDK, filesystem, subprocess, model, or device work safe; isolate blocking work in a bounded worker or the declared asynchronous job path.
Use bounded single-flight or queues, deadlines, cancellation, and one lifecycle owner for every background execution resource.
Do not perform admission, external IO, or durable writes from EventBus subscription callbacks without the explicit governed operation boundary.

items.title: Conversation, localization, and Pending Actions
rules: Keep user-visible text in declared localization contracts and preserve UTF-8 input exactly.
Conversational ambiguity requires bounded clarification; it must not silently change the requested action or enter Builder planning.
Use governed Pending Actions for consequential confirmation and preserve channel-neutral semantics across UI, voice, and Telegram.

items.title: Root-accounted asynchronous LLM work
rules: Submit long or Builder-like model work through the Root-accounted async LLM job SDK, persist its job_id, and resume by polling; use synchronous calls only for bounded short work.
Validate model output against the admitted schema before applying it, and retain provider usage and failure evidence for Subscription accounting.
Do not call model providers directly or introduce an unmetered fallback path.

items.title: Member and subnet-aware handling
rules: Derive member and device identity from trusted event or routing metadata; never accept caller-selected ownership or hardcode the local node.
Bound per-receiver payload and subnet fanout, and represent dormant, disconnected, partial, and stale member data explicitly.
Coalesce high-frequency membership updates and keep handlers idempotent across reconnect and replay.

items.title: Resource access and privacy boundary
rules: Enforce authorization in the provider or public API, not only by hiding UI actions; derive actor, subject, delegation, and ownership from trusted context.
Declare redaction, retention, and audit behavior for sensitive fields and artifacts, and do not expose secrets in model context or evidence.
Return explicit permission-denied and unsupported-operation states without converting them into empty data or broadening access.

items.title: Exact consumer and SDK contract realization
rules: Treat admitted operation names and request/response schemas as ABI: implement and export every exact required operation, including required/const/enum/additionalProperties boundaries.
Prove compatibility through the real published consumer normalizer, validator, or conformance path; a self-authored look-alike fixture is not consumer evidence.

Run every required admitted conformance fixture against the production provider path. Keep independent contracts independent, use worker-supplied task runtime roots, and never return platform-protected environment keys.
Resolve declared working directories and expected outputs exactly, then collect and verify through the admitted operations; do not substitute an implicit path or permissive local schema.
When the public SDK/API cannot express the requirement, do not patch around core or imitate the contract locally; return the governed core-capability escalation.

items.title: Application lifecycle and publisher authority
rules: Use only `adaos.sdk.builder.applications` for authoring lifecycle and `adaos.sdk.applications` or ApplicationsPlane for product lifecycle; never import Application services, mutate registries, or address runtime filesystem paths.
Keep DEV preview in `dev/.runtime`, Trial source/runtime in the top-level `trials` tree, and stable installation/runtime in `workspace`; do not introduce alpha or place Trial state below Workspace.
Publish only an accepted immutable Candidate. First stable promotes its exact link-only Trial digest; later stable promotes the exact current prerelease digest and retires that prerelease pointer.

Bind every mutation to actor, publisher subnet, required capability, expected revision, idempotency key, and its durable operation and plan digests. An unknown outcome must be reconciled before retry.
Applications owns product inventory and Development Report UX, but do not remove Infrastate Inventory until the Applications system release has passed the replacement acceptance gate.

items.title: Governed scientific handoff
rules: Treat the accepted experiment system specification and digest as executable subject authority: preserve component settings, arm semantics, intervention boundaries, and locked invariants on the production runner path.
A bounded fixture may reduce cost only where the admitted execution profile permits; it must not substitute another model family, operator, input geometry, output space, or scientific subject.
Emit the required implementation observation from that same path so an independent consumer can detect semantic substitution.

items.title: Research runner input policy
rules: For `adaos.research.runner.v1`, select input only from the admitted `request.profile_conditions.input_policy.source`.
`deterministic_contract_fixture` runs bounded production conformance without opening the accepted dataset; `accepted_dataset` selects the admitted dataset path.
Do not add a duplicate private selector under `request.conditions` or infer dataset authority from ambient files.

items.title: Initial equivalence evidence
rules: When initial equivalence is required, test it on production operators before training with the same admitted input and shared initialization state for both arms.
Enforce the admitted tolerance directly; a declaration, parameter default, or post-training comparison is not equivalence evidence.
